newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Henkel to take control of Slovenia unit.
newsitem.headline: Henkel to take control of Slovenia unit.

text.p: Germany's Henkel KGaA has offered Slovenian trading company Zlatorog 14 million marks to take full control of its Slovenian joint venture Henkel-Zlatorog, Zlatorog said on Wednesday.
Henkel currently owns 51 percent of Henkel-Zlatorog, the rest is held by Zlatorag.
"Our board yesterday accepted a proposal of our management to sell the stake and shareholders are expected to approve the move on Friday," Zlatorag chief executive Dragan Graorac told Reuters.
"We want to sell our stake because we are not a real strategic partner to Henkel and because we want to invest into other areas," Graorac said.
In March, Henkel-Zlatorog reported 1996 revenues of 9.6 billion tolars, up 3.2 percent from a year ago.

Zlatorog, which is listed on the over-the-counter market of the Ljubljana bourse, was last traded on May 14 when it fell 1.26 percent to 8,000 tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
